annotations.text:
Three homepages, same content and the same real Ramat Aviv data — only the visual language differs. Pick one.

Each carries a Sunset toggle: off is the normal state (46 min left), on is shkia approaching, where the time and countdown warm to coral with 8 min left.

The desktop artboard shows direction A at full width. Whichever you pick gets the same treatment.

Note on B: Florentin's ground IS kurkar sand — that is the direction, not a decoration. So it does not fit a strict white / sea / sunset palette. If those three colours are firm, B is out by definition and the real choice is A or C.
In all three, הרמב״ם is the honest row: the source says only "בזמן", so it shows as unknown with a prompt to correct it — never a guessed time. Compare how loudly each direction treats an absence.
